provenance.summary: These labels are NOT independent of Jev. The v1 labeller saw Jev's captured spine and family choices (and their probabilities) for every item while it labelled, and two v1 verdicts were later changed after the router missed those items. Read the details below before treating a score against this file as an accuracy measurement.

v1.note: Byte-for-byte copy of the original labelling output. It uses the labeller's placeholder names for the three new families (search-match, content-sub, mission); this file maps them to listings, publication and nonprofit (see aliases).
v1.labeller: claude-sonnet-5 agent. It wrote one hand-judged decision per item into a Python script (spines, archetypes, acceptable families, reason) that built the file.
saw: packages/agency-fast-lane/tests/fixtures/route-corpus-25.json as it was then (captured against the 10-family registry): Jev's spine, skin, family and archetype choices with confidences and probabilities for all 25 items
the 25 design-index profiles: structured catalog fields only (title, category, vertical, use_case, niche, catalog_action, motion_level) plus each profile's own Jev route choice

shape-atlas.json (spines, archetypes, compatibility matrix) and family-registry.json with the 10 families and their summaries as of 2026-09-23, before commit 9fb21de47c rewrote the emmpo and fervor summaries
didNotSee: any prose brief or MotionSites prompt text (none exists in the corpus; the prompt text is quota-gated)
the listings, publication and nonprofit families as built: it labelled against assumed placeholders (search-match on SM.01, content-sub on CS.01, mission on MI.01); listings shipped on SM.02
any score from this eval: the first live eval run is 2026-09-24T00:01Z, after the labels
v1.jevSignal: Jev's spine and family choice is copied into every item's sourceMeta (jev_spine, jev_family), and three items' reasons cite Jev's answer or confidence (dreamcore-landing, mostar-guide, prisma-landing). The labelling note calls Jev's choice "one signal among several, not ground truth". The artefacts cannot show how much that signal moved any verdict, so the labels are not blind to the router's input.
v1.illegalFamilies: Derived mechanically from the atlas compatibility matrix (transfer < 2), not judged, and not affected by what the labeller saw.
v1.labelingNote: The top-level labelingNote is the labeller's own text, kept verbatim from v1. Its phrase "built independently" is qualified by jevSignal below.

v2.adjudication: evals/genui/fixtures/route-corpus-adjudication-2026-09-23.json (written 2026-09-24T00:13Z). Each record holds only catalog evidence fields, a verdict, a confidence and reasoning; no Jev answer appears in it. The prompt given to the adjudicator is not preserved, so what else it saw cannot be confirmed from the artefacts.
v2.selection: Only two items were adjudicated, and both were misses in the live runs made before the adjudication (live-m4 at 00:01Z and live-m4-r2 at 00:02Z); both were unrouted in r2. Both changes make that unrouted outcome correct: replaying the r2 answers moves from 17/25 under v1 to 19/25 under v2. No item the router got right was re-examined, so this adjudication could only raise the score.

changed.meaning: correct when routed to publication or left unrouted

v2.unchanged: No other label changed: every other item, every illegalFamilies list (including these two), and all acceptableSpines and acceptableArchetypes are exactly as in v1.
v2.test: evals/genui/route-eval.test.ts diffs route-corpus-labels.v1.json (alias-mapped) against this file and asserts that exactly these two item fields differ.

labeller: claude-sonnet-5 (v1 labeller; not blind to Jev, see provenance.v1)

newFamilies.rationale: 'search-match' names the two-sided discover-then-match pattern (query, filter, compare, inspect, transact). SM.01 Marketplace (freelancer/rental/provider/resale matching) captures that better than the narrower SM.02 Directory, SM.03 Real estate, SM.04 Jobs, or SM.05 Comparison archetypes, all of which are marketplace sub-cases.

'content-sub' = content subscription. CS.01 Publication or media (magazine/news/editorial, discover-consume-subscribe-return) is a direct, unambiguous match; CS.02/CS.03 are documentation/research-library variants, a narrower fit for the family name.

MI.01 Nonprofit or charity is the broader, more general MI archetype ('turn concern into contribution') matching a family named simply 'mission'; MI.02 Advocacy or campaign is the narrower political/petition sub-case.

labelingNote: The route-corpus fixture (tests/fixtures/route-corpus-25.json) stores only Jev's own captured route answers (spine/skin/family/archetype choices + probabilities), not prose briefs. The matching design-index profiles at Mishh-Agency-Restored-2026-09-16/.../route/catalog-25-v2/profiles/*.json are themselves design-index profiles (per task point 1's fallback instruction), also with no prose brief field — each profile's 'source' points to a MotionSites prompt id/title only. Raw MotionSites prompt text is gated (3 free full-text reads per account via mcp__motionsites__get_prompt), so labels below were built independently from each profile's structured label fields (title, category, vertical, use_case, niche, catalog_action, motion_level, section/style scores) rather than from Jev's own route/family choice, which was treated as one signal among several, not ground truth. Several items (prisma-landing, mindloop-landing, mostar-guide) were judged to disagree with Jev's own spine or family pick; this is flagged per-item in 'reason'.
